abstract: The author reviews highlights of advances in knowledge concerning ovarian tumor pathology since the time of an essay in the first issue of this Journal written by Dr Robert E. Scully, who, both before and for several decades after the Journal was instituted, made many original contributions to the field and was the major architect of the 1973 World Health Organization classification of ovarian tumors which was much more clear and logical than prior ones. The current review considers the neoplasms in essentially the same order as was done in the first issue of this journal and presents a personal look at the highlights of new information concerning various well-known categories, surface epithelial, germ cell, sex cord-stromal, metastatic neoplasms and briefly, benign so-called tumor-like lesions. Some of the most notable developments are as follows: (1) an orderly approach to the classification of implants of serous borderline tumors into noninvasive and invasive categories; (2) recognition of distinctive micropapillary patterns seen in some borderline tumors and low-grade carcinomas; (3) a remarkable propensity for some endometrioid carcinomas to mimic sex cord- stromal tumors; (4) appreciation of the differences between primary mucinous tumors of intestinal and müllerian types; (5) the importance of distinguishing within primary mucinous carcinomas between expansile and destructive stromal invasion; (6) emphasis on the diagnosis of immature teratoma being based on the presence of primitive-embryonic-appearing tissues; (7) appreciation of variant morphology of cases of struma ovarii which may lead to significant diagnostic problems; (8) subdivision of granulosa cell tumors into adult and juvenile types because of the differing features of the two groups including in the second category the propensity for more malignant neoplasms to be mimicked; (9) recognition of a distinctive form of Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, the retiform variant, with a propensity to occur in the young; (10) appreciation of a unique highly malignant neoplasm that typically afflicts the young and may be associated with hypercalcemia, so-called small cell carcinoma of hypercalcemic type; (11) greater awareness than was hitherto the case of the propensity for metastatic intestinal adenocarcinoma to mimic primary endometrioid carcinoma and similarly for metastatic mucinous carcinomas to simulate primary mucinous cystic tumors; (12) recognition of the distinctive features of low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms that spread to the ovary and are typically associated with pseudomyxoma peritonei; and (13) appreciation that the histologic spectrum seen in cases of Krukenberg tumor is broader than often previously thought.
abstract_ja:
著者は、本誌の創刊号に掲載されたRobert E. Scully博士の論文以降の卵巣腫瘍病理学に関する知見の進歩のハイライトをまとめている。Scully博士は、雑誌創刊の前後数十年にわたり、この分野に多くの独創的な貢献をし、1973年に世界保健機関(WHO)が定めた卵巣腫瘍分類の主要な策定者であり、その分類は従来のものよりはるかに明確で論理的であった。本総説は、本誌創刊号と同じ順序で腫瘍を取り上げ、表層上皮性、胚細胞性、性索間質性、転移性腫瘍、ならびに良性のいわゆる腫瘍様病変といった、よく知られた各カテゴリーについて、新たな情報のハイライトを個人的な視点から紹介する。

注目すべき進展は以下のとおりである。(1)漿液性境界悪性腫瘍の播種病変を非浸潤性と浸潤性のカテゴリーに分類する体系的なアプローチ、(2)一部の境界悪性腫瘍および低悪性度癌で認められる特徴的な微小乳頭状パターンの認識、(3)一部の類内膜癌が性索間質性腫瘍を模倣する顕著な傾向、(4)腸型と müllerian 型の原発性粘液性腫瘍の違いの認識、(5)原発性粘液性癌において、膨張性と破壊性の間質浸潤を区別することの重要性、(6)未熟奇形腫の診断は原始・胎生様の組織の存在に基づくべきであることの強調、(7)卵巣甲状腺腫の多様な形態の認識(重大な診断上の問題を生じうる)、(8)顆粒膜細胞腫を成人型と若年型に細分類すること(両群の特徴の違いによる。後者では、より悪性度の高い腫瘍が模倣されやすい傾向を含む)、(9)網状変異型という特徴的な型の Sertoli-Leydig 細胞腫の認識(若年者に生じやすい)、(10)高カルシウム血症を伴うことがある、若年者に好発する特異的で極めて悪性度の高い腫瘍、いわゆる高カルシウム血症型小細胞癌の認識、(11)転移性腸管腺癌が原発性類内膜癌を模倣し、同様に転移性粘液性癌が原発性粘液性嚢胞性腫瘍を模倣することへの、これまで以上の認識、(12)卵巣に進展し、典型的には偽粘液腫(腹膜偽粘液腫)を伴う低悪性度虫垂粘液性腫瘍の特徴の認識、(13)クルッケンベルグ腫瘍で認められる組織学的スペクトラムは、従来考えられていたより広いことの認識。
